raw_case_text:
A 48-year-old male was referred to our hospital with severe headaches, bilateral hearing loss, and psychosis. His symptoms had started 6 months earlier with intermittent fever and headache accompanied by fatigue and asthenia. Over the course of 2 months, he developed arthralgia, osphyalgia, erythematous papular lesions, and psychosis. At a local hospital, magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) revealed signals in the right frontal cortex and subcortical white matter that were abnormally slightly thickened and strengthened near the meninges. Lumbar puncture revealed that the cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) protein level was 1.04 g/L (normal range, 0.15-0.45 g/L); leukocyte count, 41 x106/L; mononuclear cells, 82%; and glucose, 3.47 mmol/L (reference, 2.5-4.4 mmol/L). CSF Gram staining, acid-fast bacilli staining, and potassium hydroxide preparation results did not suggest a bacterial or fungal etiology. The patient was diagnosed with viral meningoencephalitis and underwent treatment with acyclovir and dexamethasone. After 10 days, his neurological symptoms did not improve, so he was referred to our hospital.
At our hospital, neurological examination revealed bilateral hearing loss and positive meningeal stimulation. Hearing examination suggested frequency-induced hearing loss at 1000-8000 Hz. The results of other examinations at this time were within normal limits. Lumbar puncture revealed clear CSF. The CSF leukocyte count was 81 x106/L (89% lymphocytes); CSF protein level, 1.36 g/L (normal range, 0.15-0.45 g/L); and glucose level, within normal range. The CSF was negative for oligoclonal bands. The CSF pathogen microbial-targeted gene surveillance result was positive (103 copies/mL), while the CSF cryptococcal antigen test and polymerase chain reaction for Mycobacterium tuberculosis yielded negative results. Blood and CSF cultures subsequently showed the growth of Brucella species ( Table 1 ).
As with the local hospital MRI, enhanced brain MRI at our hospital revealed hyperintense lesions on T2WI involving the right frontal cortex and subcortical white matter that were abnormally slightly thickened and strengthened near the meninges ( Figure 1 ).
The patient also had a history of being bitten by sheep. He was treated with ceftriaxone, rifampicin (900 mg once daily), and doxycycline (100 mg twice daily) for 12 weeks. At the 6-mo follow-up, he was asymptomatic, blood cultures were negative, and the brain lesions seen on MRI disappeared.

subjective.chief_complaint: A 48-year-old male presented with a 6-month history of intermittent fever and severe headaches, complicated over the last 4 months by bilateral hearing loss and psychosis.
subjective.history_of_present_illness: A 48-year-old male developed intermittent fever, severe headaches, fatigue, and asthenia 6 months prior to referral. Within 2 months of symptom onset, he developed arthralgia, low back pain (osphyalgia), erythematous papular skin lesions, bilateral hearing loss, and psychosis. At a local hospital, brain MRI showed right frontal cortical/subcortical meningeal thickening and enhancement, and CSF analysis showed protein 1.04 g/L, WBC 41 x 10^6/L (82% mononuclear), and glucose 3.47 mmol/L with negative Gram, AFB, and KOH stains; 10 days of acyclovir and dexamethasone for presumed viral meningoencephalitis failed to improve his symptoms, prompting referral.
subjective.past_medical_history: History of being bitten by a sheep; prior 10-day local hospitalization treated with acyclovir and dexamethasone.
subjective.review_of_systems: Positive for severe headache, bilateral hearing loss, psychosis, intermittent fever, fatigue, asthenia, arthralgia, low back pain, and erythematous papular rash.

objective.physical_examination: Bilateral sensorineural hearing loss and positive meningeal irritation signs; remainder of physical examination within normal limits.
objective.routine_investigations: Pure-tone audiometry demonstrated high-frequency sensorineural hearing loss at 1000-8000 Hz; routine hematological and biochemical tests were within normal limits.
objective.advanced_workup: Repeat lumbar puncture yielded clear CSF with WBC 81 x 10^6/L (89% lymphocytes), elevated protein 1.36 g/L (normal: 0.15-0.45 g/L), normal glucose, negative oligoclonal bands, and negative CSF cryptococcal antigen and Mycobacterium tuberculosis PCR. Contrast-enhanced brain MRI confirmed T2-weighted hyperintense lesions in the right frontal cortex and subcortical white matter with adjacent meningeal thickening and enhancement.

assessment_and_plan.assessment_and_confirmation: CSF targeted microbial gene surveillance was positive for Brucella (103 copies/mL), and both blood and CSF cultures grew Brucella species, confirming neurobrucellosis meningoencephalitis. Treated with ceftriaxone, oral rifampicin (900 mg QD), and oral doxycycline (100 mg BID) for 12 weeks. At 6-month follow-up, the patient was completely asymptomatic with negative blood cultures and complete resolution of brain MRI lesions.
